rationale.conceptual: The method involves an established but non-trivial combination of DFT, phonon calculations, four different CALPHAD liquid models (associate, ionic, two MQMQA variants), and Bayesian model selection via MCMC. Successfully implementing all components requires deep domain knowledge in computational thermodynamics and several interacting mathematical formulations.
rationale.execution: The pipeline has more than 7 stages: configurational search, DFT relaxations, energy-volume scans, phonon supercell calculations, EOS fitting, thermodynamic derivation, CALPHAD input assembly from multiple experimental sources, MCMC for four binary models and one ternary model. It involves multiple independent tools (ATAT, Quantum ESPRESSO, Phonopy, ESPEI, PyCalphad) with fragile handoffs.

difficulty.reasoning: The paper combines first-principles DFT+phonon calculations and CALPHAD thermodynamic modeling across four compounds, comparing four liquid models using Bayesian model selection. The conceptual difficulty is high due to the need for genuine understanding of multiple interacting components (DFT, phonon, CALPHAD models, MCMC). Execution is lengthy and multi-tool (ATAT, Quantum ESPRESSO, Phonopy, ESPEI, PyCalphad), requiring careful orchestration and data assembly. Resource needs mirror the original paper: DFT supercell calculations on HPC, but no GPU required.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Original work used VASP on university HPC (NERSC) for DFT+phonon calculations on up to 64-atom supercells. Memory per node likely 32–64 GB. Input data are only crystal structures and pseudopotentials, so data volume is negligible.
